desc:
You own a purse of coins with positive integer values, given in sorted (non-decreasing) order in coins. You want every integer amount from 1 to n to be payable exactly using some sub-collection of your coins (each coin used at most once).

You may add new coins of any positive integer value to the purse. Return the minimum number of coins you must add so that all amounts 1..n become payable.

coins = [1, 3], n = 6        -> 1   (add 2)
coins = [1, 5, 10], n = 20   -> 2   (add 2 and 4)
coins = [1, 2, 2], n = 5     -> 0
hints: Keep track of reach: the largest value such that every amount in [1, reach] can already be paid.
If the next coin is at most reach + 1, then it extends the covered range to reach + coin. Otherwise there is a gap right after reach.
To close the gap at reach + 1 the best coin you can add has value exactly reach + 1: it doubles the covered range. Add it (count a patch) and check the same coin again. Stop once reach ≥ n.
editorial: Let reach be the largest value such that all of 1..reach is payable with the coins processed (or added) so far; initially 0. Look at the next coin c (in sorted order). If c ≤ reach + 1, we can pay reach + 1 .. reach + c by combining c with an amount from the covered range, so reach += c and we move on.

Otherwise the amount reach + 1 is unpayable, and no existing coin can help (they are all larger). We must add a coin of value at most reach + 1; choosing exactly reach + 1 is best because it extends the range the most, to 2 * reach + 1. Count a patch, update reach and look at the same coin again. When the coins run out, keep patching while reach < n.

Each patch at least doubles reach, so there are at most about 31 patches, and every coin is looked at once: O(m + log n) time. Note that the covered range can exceed 231 inside the loop; Python integers do not care, but in fixed-width languages use 64 bits.
